Extract values from netCDFs to one or more point observations

Source: R/extract_to_points.R
extract_to_point.Rd

This is the general point-extraction interface. It can extract environmental values for one or multiple observations. The user chooses the type of extraction with the method argument. The more specific functions extract2d(), extract3d_surface(), extract3d_bottom(), extract3d_nearest() and extract3d_all() are wrappers around this function.

Usage

extract_to_point(
  data = NULL,
  nc,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  depth = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  method = c("2d", "surface", "bottom", "nearest", "all"),
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  date_col = "date",
  depth_col = "depth",
  id_col = NULL,
  file_col = "file",
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  output_prefix = NULL,
  output_col = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  time_resolution = c("auto", "datetime", "daily", "monthly", "yearly", "custom"),
  custom_time_interval = NULL,
  time_report = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Optional object containing observation points. Can be a data frame, tibble, sf object with POINT geometries, matrix with column names, or named list. If NULL, coordinates can be supplied directly through lon, lat, and optionally depth and date. For sf objects, longitude and latitude are obtained from the POINT geometries; projected geometries are transformed internally to longitude and latitude when a CRS is available.

nc

netCDF source. Can be a file path, vector of file paths, list of file paths, opened ncdf4 object, list of opened objects, or a data frame with a file column.

lon

Optional numeric longitude value or vector for direct point extraction when data = NULL.

lat

Optional numeric latitude value or vector for direct point extraction when data = NULL.

depth

Optional numeric observation depth value or vector for direct point extraction. Required when data = NULL and method = "nearest" or method = "all".

date

Optional observation date or vector of dates for direct point extraction. Used when data = NULL and the netCDF variable has a time dimension. Accepts Date and POSIXt objects, or character values in "YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" format (UTC). Direct input vectors may have length 1 or a common compatible length.

var

Name of the variable to extract from the netCDF file. If NULL, the function tries to detect the variable automatically from each file. This only works when each netCDF file contains one single variable.

method

Extraction method. Options are "2d", "surface", "bottom", "nearest" and "all". With method = "all", the function returns nearest, surface and bottom outputs together.

lon_col

Name of the longitude column in data.

lat_col

Name of the latitude column in data.

date_col

Name of the date column in data. Required only when the netCDF variable has a time dimension.

depth_col

Name of the observation-depth column in data. Required only when method = "nearest" or method = "all".

id_col

Optional observation identifier column. It is not required for extraction, but it is checked when provided to help users detect mistakes.

file_col

Column containing file paths when nc is a data frame.

lon_dim

Optional name of the longitude dimension in the netCDF file.

lat_dim

Optional name of the latitude dimension in the netCDF file.

depth_dim

Optional name of the depth dimension in the netCDF file.

time_dim

Optional name of the time dimension in the netCDF file.

time_match

Character. How observation dates are matched to netCDF time values. "nearest" (default) selects the closest available date; "exact" requires an exact date match and returns NA when no match exists.

max_time_diff

Optional non-negative numeric value giving the maximum allowed difference, in days, between an observation date and the nearest netCDF date when time_match = "nearest". If NULL (default), no maximum temporal distance is imposed. Ignored when time_match = "exact".

output_prefix

Optional name used for the extracted output column. If omitted, var is used.

output_col

Optional alias for output_prefix. Use this when you want to define the exact name of the output column directly. If both output_col and output_prefix are provided, output_col is used. With method = "all", this name is used as the suffix in nearest_*, surface_* and seabottom_* columns.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, progress messages are printed every 100 rows.

time_resolution

Precision used to compare observation times with dataset timestamps. "auto" uses daily comparison for Date objects and date-only text, and datetime comparison for POSIXt objects and date-time text. Explicit alternatives are "datetime", "daily", "monthly", "yearly" and "custom". Calendar comparisons use UTC. These options compare timestamp labels; they do not infer averaging intervals or calculate temporal summaries. Multiple dataset records mapping to the same comparison value cause an error. With nearest matching, monthly and yearly comparisons use the start of the labelled month or year. max_time_diff remains in days and applies to these comparison values. Use exact matching to require the same labelled day, month or year.

custom_time_interval

Positive difftime value used as the warning interval when time_resolution = "custom". Matching uses full timestamps. This interval does not reject candidates; use max_time_diff for that.

time_report

Logical. If TRUE, the default, display a temporal summary when returned values are displaced in time or outputs are missing. The return format is unchanged. FALSE hides the summary but does not suppress temporal warnings.

Value

If data is provided, the input observations with extracted values appended. Data frames, tibbles and sf objects retain their structure; matrices and named lists are returned as data frames. If data = NULL, direct extraction returns a numeric value for one point and one output, a numeric vector for multiple points and one output, a named numeric vector for one point and multiple outputs (for example, method = "all"), or a data frame for multiple points and multiple outputs.

Details

Numeric netCDF time coordinates must provide units expressed as milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days since a reference date-time. Singular and plural unit names are accepted.

Reference date-times are interpreted in UTC. A trailing "Z" or "UTC" is accepted; numeric timezone offsets such as "+02:00" are not currently supported.

Supported calendars are "standard", "gregorian" and "proleptic_gregorian". The first two are supported only for reference dates and timestamps on or after 1582-10-15. Unsupported units, calendars or missing time units produce an error.

Temporal resolution controls comparison of timestamp labels. It does not identify averaging intervals, calculate temporal means, or interpret climatological periods.

Multiple sources

With multiple sources, only cells containing the observation are eligible. Explicit spatial cell bounds are preferred. Otherwise, edges are inferred from adjacent centres; singleton axes without bounds require coincidence. Longitude comparisons support equivalent coordinates across the antimeridian. Among eligible sources the closest temporal candidate with a valid value wins, with input order breaking ties. Existing output columns are replaced, including by NA. Output names cannot overwrite extraction inputs or combine different variables in the same column.

Custom temporal intervals

With time_resolution = "custom", observations require hours as for datetime. For example, custom_time_interval = as.difftime(3, units = "hours") warns above three hours of displacement. Exact matching requires the same timestamp. Auto matching remains unchanged and uses the observed cadence for diagnostics.

Temporal diagnostics

Diagnostics are emitted after source selection, for values actually returned. Daily, monthly and yearly comparisons warn on a change of calendar period in UTC. Datetime comparisons warn when displacement exceeds one observed cadence step, or when a nonzero displacement has no reliable cadence. With a detected daily cadence, datetime comparison also warns when the selected value falls on a different UTC day, even below 24 hours. Explanatory warnings include the requested and selected timestamps, their difference, the comparison resolution, cadence, row, variable and file name. Reports explain non-warning displacements and missing outputs without repeating examples already explained by a temporal warning. Cadence inference does not change matching or impose a maximum time gap. Singleton sources may use the observed sequence of compatible files for the same variable. Time bounds describe intervals, not sampling frequency.

Examples

nc_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_3d.nc",
  package = "ocean3d"
)

# Extract the value closest to a single observation
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file,
  lon = 0,
  lat = 40,
  depth = 60,
  date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp",
  method = "nearest"
)
#> [1] 15.5

# Extract values for multiple observations
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file,
  lon = c(0, 1),
  lat = c(40, 41),
  depth = c(60, 100),
  date = "2020-01-03",
  var = "temp",
  method = "nearest"
)
#> [1] 15.5 13.5

# Match a complete observation timestamp.
# The example file has a reading at midnight on 2020-01-03.
extract_to_point(
  nc = nc_file,
  lon = 0,
  lat = 40,
  depth = 60,
  date = as.POSIXct("2020-01-03 00:15:00", tz = "UTC"),
  var = "temp",
  method = "nearest",
  time_resolution = "datetime",
  max_time_diff = 30 / 1440
)
#> Warning: Temporal warning: 1 observation(s) need attention.
#> 
#> A different timestamp was selected, but its cadence is unknown.
#> Row 1; variable: temp; output: temp.
#> Observation: 2020-01-03 00:15:00 UTC
#> Selected data: 2020-01-03 00:00:00 UTC
#> Difference: 15 minutes earlier.
#> Comparison resolution: datetime.
#> Detected cadence: irregular; no reliable sampling interval.
#> The available timestamps do not establish a reliable sampling interval. The time difference cannot be assessed against a detected cadence. Use time_resolution = 'custom' with custom_time_interval if you know the appropriate warning interval.
#> File: example_3d.nc
#> [1] 15.5

# Compare monthly labels when the file has one record per month.
# Here the timestamp labels are illustrative.
monthly_labels <- as.Date(c("2020-01-15", "2020-02-15"))
observation_date <- as.Date("2020-02-28")
format(monthly_labels, "%Y-%m") ==
  format(observation_date, "%Y-%m")
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE

# For extraction from such a file, use:
# time_resolution = "monthly", time_match = "exact".
# Multiple records in the same month cause an error;
# they are not averaged automatically.
